# Summary of British National Party Manifesto 2010

The BNP 2010 Manifesto presents a comprehensive nationalist programme centered on preserving Britain's indigenous population, culture, and sovereignty against what it characterizes as existential threats from mass immigration, the European Union, and Islamic colonisation.

## Core Ideological Premise

The manifesto argues that current immigration and birth rates will render indigenous British people a minority within decades, constituting "extinction" of British culture, heritage, and identity. It positions the BNP as the only party willing to address this crisis honestly.

## Immigration and Demographics

The party proposes halting all further immigration, deporting illegal immigrants and foreign criminals, ending the "asylum swindle," and promoting voluntary repatriation with financial incentives. It would review all citizenship grants since 1997, accusing Labour of deliberately engineering mass immigration to change Britain's demographics. The manifesto calls for repealing the Race Relations Act and abolishing "politically correct" social engineering, including the Equalities and Human Rights Commission.

## Counter-Jihad

Islam is characterized as fundamentally incompatible with Western democracy and a colonising force. Proposed measures include banning the burka, ritual slaughter, and mosque construction; halting all Muslim immigration; and deporting radical preachers and their followers. The party identifies mass immigration and biased foreign policy as twin causes of Islamist terrorism.

## European Union

The BNP demands immediate EU withdrawal, characterizing it as an Orwellian superstate usurping British sovereignty. Savings from membership fees would fund domestic infrastructure and poverty alleviation.

## Economy and Welfare

The manifesto proposes cutting expenditure on "global warming" measures, foreign aid, EU membership, and foreign wars to address national debt without reducing front-line services. It advocates raising personal tax allowances, reintroducing married man's allowances, protecting British industry through tariffs, and ensuring welfare benefits only reach those who have contributed to the system.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

The party would withdraw troops from Afghanistan, avoid war with Iran, renegotiate NATO membership, and pursue a neutral foreign policy putting British interests first, including reaching accord with Muslim nations in exchange for halting Islamic immigration.

## Civil Liberties and Culture

The manifesto calls for repealing restrictions on free speech, rejecting ID cards, withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights, and restoring traditional British values in education and public life.
